title: Vital phenomena cannot be cleanly divided into physical and non-physical ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Vital phenomena cannot be cleanly divided into physical and non-physical ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: There is no clear rule for deciding what is 'vital', and the properties of organisms cannot be clearly split into those of physical origin and those peculiar to living things, so physical analysis must proceed piece by piece.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is plain that we have no clear rule or guide as to what is “vital” and what is not; the whole assemblage of so-called vital phenomena, or properties of the organism, cannot be clearly classified into those that are physical in origin and those that are _sui generis_ and peculiar to living things.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Vital versus physical phenomena”. Scope: properties and processes of living organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-08: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.11

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a conceptual claim about classification and research strategy. Particular processes can be physically modelled, but their success cannot establish that no clear global division exists.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: No dataset can uniquely decide whether a phenomenon belongs to a clearly bounded vital or physical category without first imposing the classification whose absence the claim asserts.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The asserted lack of a clean taxonomy is methodological rather than observational.

Vital is undefined.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a conceptual claim about categories. No dataset of organismal properties can show that a clear vital-versus-physical rule is impossible, because any proposed rule can be rejected as unclear without a measurable consequence that separates the claim from a rival rule.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim asserts that there is no clear rule dividing vital from physical properties. A survey of how biologists classify phenomena would describe usage, not confirm or refute the absence of a rule.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Denying a classification does not specify a distinguishing measurement.
